title: Operator playbook for streamed schema handshake and tool-repair acceptance
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create an acceptance-oriented operator/playbook artifact and concrete acceptance criteria for streamed structured output that includes tool/function calling. Focus is on observable handshakes, resumability tokens, graded validation, repair flows for partial or malformed fragments, and operational runbooks for SREs and support engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake: Every streamed response with a tool invocation must begin with a deterministic handshake frame that includes: schema_version, request_id, resumability_token (optional), and declared_required_tools; failure to emit handshake within 200ms of first byte is recorded as handshake_timeout.

Fragment envelopes: Each emitted fragment must be wrapped with an explicit envelope header containing fragment_index, fragment_length_estimate (if known), and cumulative_checksum. Consumers must be able to detect missing fragments and request replay via resumability_token.

Partial-object semantics: If a fragment contains a partial object (e.g., a partially emitted JSON field), receiver must treat it as 'repairable' when the schema anchor exists and the runtime must provide a repair_hint frame with suggested completion or a patch token.

Tool-call idempotency: Tool invocation frames must include an invocation_id and idempotency_key. Acceptance requires that retries with same idempotency_key are deduplicated by tool gateways and produce identical observable side-effects or return an explicit deduplication response code.

Error taxonomy: Define and implement explicit streaming error codes surfaced in envelope footers: E-HANDSHAKE, E-FRAGMENT-TRUNC, E-SCHEMA-MISMATCH, E-TOOL-FAIL, E-BACKPRESSURE. Each code must map to an operator remediation action in the playbook.

Backpressure & flow-control: The protocol must support consumer-issued window-update frames and server-respectful backpressure signals. Acceptance requires that the runtime honors window updates within 50ms and, when overloaded, emits E-BACKPRESSURE with an estimated retry-after value.

Resumability: When a stream is interrupted, the resumability_token from the handshake must allow an identical stream to be resumed (within retention window) and deliver missing fragments without duplicating already committed fragments. Tests must verify resume with network partition and client reconnect.

Observability: Each stream must emit traceable telemetry: handshake_latency_ms, fragments_emitted, fragments_repaired, tool_invocations, tool_deduped, resume_attempts, and stream_error_code. Metrics must be available per-tenant, per-model, and per-route within the console.

Validation tiers: Runtime must support three validation tiers for streamed schema enforcement: strict (reject on first deviation), tolerant (emit E-SCHEMA-MISMATCH and continue with repair_hint), and best-effort (log only). Acceptance requires tests covering each tier.

Operator playbook: For each error code include: detection steps, immediate mitigation (auto-fallback to textual-only mode or model-variant), remediation steps (replay, manual repair with patch token), and customer communication templates. Playbook must be reviewed and signed by SRE and Support.

Telemetry retention: Detailed per-stream traces for handshake+fragments must be persisted for at least 7 days for P1 incidents and 30 days for P0 incidents. Acceptance requires console drilldown from stream trace to raw fragment payloads (redacted per PII rules).
test_cases: E2E resume test: Start a 20-fragment stream with declared schema, drop packets after fragment 8, reconnect with resumability_token, and assert fragments 9-20 are delivered without reapplying side-effects of tool invocations for fragments 1-8.

Schema drift test: Emit a stream where fragment 6 changes a required field type. Validate behavior under strict, tolerant, and best-effort validation tiers and assert emitted error codes and repair_hints.

Tool idempotency test: Simulate client retry of tool invocation with same idempotency_key across network blips; verify tool gateway returns deduplicated response and no double side-effects in downstream systems.
Backpressure test: Flood server with high-concurrency small-window clients; assert server emits E-BACKPRESSURE and honors window updates after cooldown without data loss.

Malformed fragment test: Inject a truncated fragment (mid-JSON) and validate that runtime emits E-FRAGMENT-TRUNC and repair_hint; consumer applies patch token and completes object successfully in 95% of trials.
Observability test: Trigger a controlled handshake timeout and verify trace contains handshake frame, timeout event, affected request_id, and associated remediation playbook link in console.

Security/PII redaction test: Stream containing simulated PII fields should still allow fragment-level debugging with redacted_payloads accessible to SRE role; assert redaction rules applied consistently.
success_metrics: <1% of streams end in unrecoverable E-FRAGMENT-TRUNC after rollout
Resumability success rate >= 99.5% within 3 reconnect attempts
Mean time to mitigation (operator action triggered by playbook) < 15 minutes for P1 incidents
>= 95% of schema-mismatch events include a generated repair_hint frame
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind 'streamed_schema_playbook' initially on internal-only for 2 weeks
Stage 2: opt-in external beta for 10 customers with high streaming usage; collect telemetry and SRE feedback
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% of production traffic with automated rollback on metric regression
Post-rollout: run tabletop incident exercise with Support and SRE using two recorded real incidents and update playbook
notes: This artifact sits at the intersection of product, SRE, and API design; early engagement with legal for telemetry retention and redaction requirements is recommended.
Design trade-off: including resumability_token in handshake increases traceability but may increase privacy surface; consider rotating tokens per-request when PII-sensitive workloads are detected.
Operator templates should include pre-written customer-facing messages and an internal checklist to run during incident postmortems.
